title: Control drift across a generated timeline
description: Choose a temporal strategy, scene difficulty, anchor spacing, and incident. Watch identity, motion, seam risk, retry scope, and relative compute change together.

strategies.label: Independent frames
strategies.detail: Each frame sees the prompt but no neighboring latent state.
strategies.retryScope: A frame can be retried, but the surrounding motion contract is missing.
strategies.lesson: Prompt similarity does not create timeline continuity. Independent frames are a useful counterexample, not a production default.

strategies.label: Overlapping windows
strategies.detail: Each window reuses boundary frames and temporal state from the previous window.
strategies.retryScope: Retry one failed window plus its overlap boundary.
strategies.lesson: Overlap creates an explicit continuity boundary and gives retries a bounded unit of work.

strategies.label: Storyboard and identity anchors
strategies.detail: Approved keyframes, entity references, and shot boundaries constrain each window.
strategies.retryScope: Regenerate one shot and validate the incoming and outgoing transitions.
strategies.lesson: Long-form consistency comes from planned state and bounded shots, not one unlimited context window.

incidents.label: Identity after occlusion
incidents.detail: The subject disappears briefly and returns with changed attributes.

incidents.label: Worker lost at boundary

incidents.detail: A temporal combination violates policy although sampled thumbnails look acceptable.
